title: Thirteen Winters and One Short Bench
subtitle: 艺术殿堂 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 艺术殿堂（人与社会·文学、艺术与体育）
meta: 主题语境：艺术殿堂（人与社会·文学、艺术与体育）　|　核心词汇：entertainment　|　正文 346 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 entertainment 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1929 my grandmother ① provided an entertainment that no neighbour in the town would have paid for, and she said the providing was the whole of the winter. The ② entertainment, meaning the show itself and not the work, ran thirteen winters and stayed unpaid in the book; an entertainment, she said, is the only thing in a town that is judged by how long it is left unpaid.

Every ③ entertainment in that town had the same short bench beside it, and the ④ entertainment at the far side, meaning the one they kept for the children and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. An entertainment, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to pay; my grandmother said the paying is the part that fills thirteen winters.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the entertainment was the whole of the evening, meaning the performance and not the show. The ⑥ entertainment, meaning the performance and not any of that, is the only thing on a stage that everybody waits for and nobody pays for; entertainment, he said, is either something you provide or the only word that means both a show and a performance. He said the performance is the part they remember.

By 1937 the ⑦ entertainment had become a line in a programme, and the programme had become an argument about the short bench. The ⑧ entertainment of the whole thing, my grandmother wrote in January, was one town and thirteen winters of paying; entertainment, she said, is either the one at the far side or the reason you learned to pay. She said the paying was never mentioned.

The ⑨ entertainment I remember is the one paid for in the programme, which ended in 1941 and is still described as the quietest in the town. An ⑩ entertainment, my mother said in 1943, is the only one that improves by being paid for; every entertainment, she said, is a performance that has agreed to look like a show. She said the performance was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 娱乐活动（指镇上每一种旁边的那一种）
B. n. 娱乐活动（指那一场本身，与劳作相对）
C. 固定搭配：provide entertainment 提供娱乐
D. n. 娱乐活动（指留给孩子的那一场）
E. n. 娱乐（抽象总称，指一个镇上的消遣之事）
F. n. 娱乐活动（指节目单上写到、被排定的那一场）
G. n. 文娱节目；演出（指舞台上人人都等却无人付钱的那样东西）
H. n. 演出（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人付钱的那种东西）

items.q: provided an entertainment that no neighbour in the town would have paid for
The entertainment, meaning the show itself and not the work
the entertainment at the far side
the entertainment was the whole of the evening
the entertainment had become a line in a programme
The entertainment of the whole thing

answers.why: provide entertainment 意为“提供娱乐”，1929 年祖母提供了一种镇上没有一位邻居肯付钱的娱乐。
entertainment 意为“娱乐活动”，指那一场本身而不是劳作，它经过了十三个冬天而在簿子上没有账目。
entertainment 意为“娱乐活动”，指镇上每一种旁边的那一种，每一种旁边都有同一条短短的长凳。
entertainment 意为“娱乐活动”，指留给孩子的那一场，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
entertainment 意为“文娱节目、演出”，指舞台上人人都等却无人付钱的那样东西，叔叔说这场演出就是那个夜晚的全部。
entertainment 意为“演出”，指人人都等却无人付钱的那种东西而不是那一场，是舞台上人人都等、却无人付钱的东西。
entertainment 意为“娱乐活动”，指节目单上写到、被排定的那一场，到 1937 年这一场成了节目单里的一行。
entertainment 意为“娱乐”，祖母一月写道，整件事的消遣之事是一个镇子和十三个冬天的付钱。
entertainment 意为“娱乐活动”，我记得的是节目单上排定的那一场，1941 年结束了，至今仍被说成镇上最安静的一场。
entertainment 为抽象总称，母亲 1943 年说，一场娱乐是唯一会因为被好好付钱而变得更好的东西。
